newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo fall ahead of opening of parliament session.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo fall ahead of opening of parliament session.

text.p: Tokyo stocks skidded sharply lower on Monday morning ahead of the convening of a new session of Japan's parliament in the afternoon, led by selling in futures contracts.

"Selling of futures contracts means the market thinks there is little for it to look forward to in the coming months, although parliament is starting today," said Tadahiro Kamogawa, general manager at Yamaichi Securities.
The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended the morning session down 466.36 points, or 2.58 percent, at 17,623.68. Its March futures were down 520 points at 17,610.
The Nikkei plunged more than 2,000 points in the first trading week of this year on worries about the Japanese economy.
It recovered by 786.39 points last week but participants remain anxious to see if the government will offer it support in the coming parliamentary session.
Late last week some market participants bought futures in the hope that the government would try to bolster the market once parliament starts.
